etymologies.etymologyHTML: From owner +‎ -ship.

definitions.definition: The state of having complete legal control of something; possession; proprietorship.

quote.citation: 1952 February, H. C. Casserley, “Permanent Wayfarings”, in Railway Magazine, page 77:
quote.text: Other evidence of former ownerships such as notice-boards, number plates, and makers' plates, are often discovered unexpectedly.  […]  It has not been used for many years, and although it was impracticable to photograph the engine in the small confines of the shed it was possible to obtain a picture of the plate which it still carries showing the former ownership.

quote.citation: 2021 November 17, Andrew Mourant, “Okehampton: a new dawn for Dartmoor”, in RAIL, number 944, page 43:
quote.text: In the summer, DCC [Devon County Council] transferred ownership of the northern part of the station to NR for a nominal £1, enabling it (and the platform) to become part of the rail network.
